page_summary:
Now Wait for Last Year is the canonical works record for PKD's novel. It preserves a single archive manifestation and gives the work a stable bibliographic home. The preserved item here is Now Wait for Last Year (1966). The archive copy runs 131 pages.

Researchers can use this entry to trace publication context, later commentary, and relationships to other works.

structure.form: novel intercutting a political/military crisis plot with a marital-collapse plot, linked through the time-displacing drug JJ-180

characters.name: Eric Sweetscent
characters.note: An artificial-organ specialist whose proximity to power (as Gino Molinari's personal physician) and accidental exposure to JJ-180 give him privileged, fragmentary access to alternate timelines of both the war and his own marriage.

characters.name: Kathy Sweetscent
characters.note: Her addiction to the time-displacing drug JJ-180 both destroys the marriage and inadvertently opens the novel's central science-fictional device.

characters.name: Gino Molinari
characters.note: Appears to be perpetually near death; revealed to survive political and military pressure through recurring psychosomatic collapse and the use of decoy doubles rather than any single continuous illness.

settings.name: Earth under Lilistar's client-state alliance
settings.note: A political and military dependency relationship the novel increasingly frames as a mistake, with Earth suffering the costs of a war chosen by its more powerful ally.

settings.name: JJ-180-induced time-slips
settings.note: Uncontrolled jumps forward and backward through the user's own life and surrounding history, giving Eric fragmentary, often contradictory knowledge of the war's possible outcomes.

motifs: Political alliance as addiction -- a bad bargain entered for short-term survival that becomes progressively harder to escape
Illness and collapse as strategy rather than pathology -- Molinari's recurring near-deaths function as a form of leverage and self-protection
Time travel as a source of more confusion than clarity -- fragmentary, contradictory knowledge of the future does not resolve the present's central dilemmas
Marital breakdown mirrored against geopolitical crisis, with personal fidelity offered as the only value stable enough to act on amid radical uncertainty
reading.significance: Now Wait for Last Year is one of Dick's most tightly constructed novels of the mid-1960s, using its time-travel device not for adventure but to dramatize epistemological paralysis: characters gain access to the future and past only in unusable, contradictory fragments, which mirrors the novel's political theme of a leader and a planet unable to act decisively despite -- or because of -- more information than they can process. Gino Molinari, closely modeled on an exhausted, self-sacrificing wartime leader, is one of Dick's most sympathetic portraits of political power as a form of ongoing physical martyrdom. The Eric-Kathy marriage plot, widely read as reflecting the strains of Dick's own marriages and amphetamine-adjacent drug experience, grounds the novel's cosmic war-and-time-travel plot in intimate, specific domestic pain.
reading.closing_note: The novel refuses to resolve either its interstellar war or its marriage plot cleanly, ending instead on Eric's choice to keep trying with Kathy -- a small, unresolved act of fidelity offered as the only available answer to a universe of unusable information.

reading_provenance.note: Close reading of the primary text plus attributed evidence from the archive. Candidate: not yet promoted to canonical.
